newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money eases back, downside seen limited.
newsitem.headline: German call money eases back, downside seen limited.

text.p: German call money rates ticked lower on Friday, easing to around 3.06 to 3.08 percent from as high as 3.10 percent in the previous session.
Traders said that despite a slight setback in daily reserve levels held at the Budnesbank, the tone of the market lent itself more to the bid than the ask side.

But speculation was taking hold that the central bank is likely to move to tighten its repo rate in the near future and was likely to ensure that call money rates would not ease much further for the moment, traders said.

The Bundesbank is due to set its next repo argreement on Tuesday, with speculation heating up that the bank may set a variable repo and allow the rate to drift higher. The repo has been fixed at 3.00 percent for a full year.

"My impression is, that the feeling that we're going to see a rate change is becoming more and more certain," said one money market trader in Frankfurt. "So I don't see (call money) rates going much lower from here."
Daily reserve levels at the Bundesbank sank to 41.1 billion marks on Thursday from 41.5 billion marks on Wednesday, while the average monthly level stood at 40.0 billion marks.

The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= rate was set at 3.10000 percent on Friday versus 3.11133 on Thursday, but the 12-month FIBOR rate rose to 3.59933 percent from 3.58958 percent previously.
